tasks.short: Investigate organisms, disease, epidemics, and antibiotic effects.

steps.what: Investigate the relationship between organisms and disease {DOCS}
Judge control of epidemics, including effects of antibiotics on microorganisms
Mark notices whose abstracts omit that organism or antibiotic

loop.input: The organism name, disease name, and antibiotic name from s1, plus each notice title and abstract.
loop.output: A keep or drop for each notice, with a phrase quoted from that abstract.
loop.check: A mark whose quoted phrase is absent from the abstract fails, and a keep that does not name the organism or the antibiotic fails.
loop.stop: One pass over the notices in hand, or two failed checks, then she reads them herself.
loop.why_not_simpler: A word match keeps notices that name the antibiotic for a different disease and drops notices that use another name for the same organism.

steps.what: Read a sample of those marks and the quoted phrase

tasks.design: The work removed is the first pass over notice titles and abstracts, which she does today: she reads each abstract and drops a notice that is not about the organism and the antibiotic she named in {DOCS}. That pass is s3. She still investigates the relationship and still judges control of epidemics, including antibiotic effects. She still re-reads a sample of notices she is unsure about. A colleague also reads a sample of the marks. The mark is not a second record, nothing is filed, and nothing is sent.
tasks.previous_blocker: Epidemic control is a judgement about people and organisms. Marking a notice is not that judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Once she names the organism, the disease, and the antibiotic, a notice abstract can be marked against those three names.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding how to control an epidemic and what an antibiotic effect means.
tasks.human_edge: She can tell a real outbreak pattern from a notice that only shares a word.
tasks.altitude: Her week still holds the investigation and the epidemic judgement. The first pass over notice abstracts is the only part that leaves, and that pass is reading she does today.

reach.learn: Which names the screen may mark, and which notices she still reads herself.

evidence.claim: A named evidence-review tool screens titles and abstracts.
A documented systematic-review screen proposed inclusion decisions on citations and compared them with human review.
Health data are a special category, and use for public health needs a basis in law.

assumptions: Today she already reads each notice abstract and drops a notice about a different organism or a different antibiotic. The 12 points on s3 are that reading.

She names the organism, the disease, and the antibiotic in s1. One extra hour per 100 baseline hours keeps those three names current when the outbreak focus changes, and that hour is not inside the reading.
She already re-reads notices she is unsure about, which is s4. A colleague spends one hour per 100 baseline hours on a second sample, and that hour is not her time.

The mark receives only the three names, not a person-linked outbreak file. The mark is not filed in the notebook she already uses, and nothing is sent. If no notices arrive, the mark does not run and the saving is zero.
unknowns: Whether the notices are public papers or outbreak files tied to a person.
research_questions: Does she already read each notice abstract herself, and are the notices public papers?

already_counted.description: The investigation, the epidemic judgement, and the sample re-read stay in her week.

incremental.description: Keep the organism, disease, and antibiotic names current when the outbreak focus changes.
A colleague reads a sample of the marks.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When no new notices arrive the first pass does not happen and the saving is zero. When a pile arrives, only that first pass is removed, and one hour goes to keeping the three names, so the high stays at 6 rather than the full 11.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare technical reports and recommendations from research outcomes.

steps.what: Prepare technical reports from the research outcomes she gathered {DOCS}
Decide recommendations based on those research outcomes
Compose report paragraphs that restate only listed outcomes

loop.input: The outcome list and the DOI list from s1.
loop.output: Paragraphs that restate listed outcomes and cite only her DOIs.
loop.check: A sentence that states a result or a number absent from her outcome list fails, and a citation whose DOI is not on her list fails.
loop.stop: One draft, or two failed checks, then she writes the paragraphs.
loop.why_not_simpler: The outcomes are prose notes, so a fixed template cannot tell a result that is hers from a result that was added.

steps.what: Reject a report sentence whose result is not listed
Tell colleagues the recommendations she settled in the room

tasks.design: The work removed is writing the report paragraphs that restate research outcomes, which she does today when she prepares the technical report in {DOCS}. She lists the outcomes and the DOIs first. The paragraphs may restate only that list and may cite only those DOIs. She still decides the recommendations and still tells colleagues in the room. The paragraphs stay as a draft she checks. This is a technical report, not a grant application and not a peer review.
tasks.previous_blocker: The recommendation is a judgement on the outcomes. Restating them is not that judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Once the outcomes and the DOIs are listed, paragraphs can restate only that list.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the recommendation and standing behind it with colleagues.
tasks.human_edge: She knows which outcome is solid enough to recommend.
tasks.altitude: She still chooses the recommendation and still tells colleagues. The first paragraphs that restate listed outcomes are the only writing that leaves.

reach.task: Prepare a technical report from shared outcomes
reach.learn: How to reject a paragraph that adds a result she did not list.

evidence.claim: A named lab-notebook product drafts study reports.
A published check of model-written bibliographies found many fabricated citations.
The national research funder bars generative models for its grant assessors and bars hidden prompts in applications.
European guidance advises against generative models in peer review and in evaluations.

assumptions: Today she writes the paragraphs that restate research outcomes before she chooses the recommendation. The 15 points on s3 are that writing.
One extra hour per 100 baseline hours keeps the outcome list and the DOI list current. That hour is not inside the listing she already does in s1.
The recommendation and the room conversation stay. The draft is a technical report, not a grant application and not a peer review, and it is not filed and not sent.
If the outcomes are not written as a list, she writes the paragraphs herself and the saving is zero.
unknowns: Whether the technical report leaves the organisation.
research_questions: Does she write the outcome paragraphs herself before the recommendation, and does the report leave the organisation?

already_counted.description: Listing outcomes, deciding the recommendation, checking sentences, and telling colleagues stay in her week.

incremental.description: Keep the outcome list and the DOI list current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the outcomes are not written as a list she writes the paragraphs herself and the saving is zero. When the list is short the draft covers only part of the writing, and one hour goes to keeping the list, so the high stays at 8.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe microorganism action on tissues, animals, and organic matter.

steps.what: Observe action of microorganisms upon living tissues of plants
Observe that action on higher animals and other microorganisms
Judge what that action did to dead organic matter
Write the observed action into the laboratory notebook {OTHER}

tasks.design: Nothing is built. She observes the action of microorganisms on living tissues of plants, on higher animals and other microorganisms, and on dead organic matter, and she writes that observation into the laboratory notebook {OTHER} she already uses. Both the watching and that single notebook entry stay. There is no second entry and no transport.
tasks.previous_blocker: What a microorganism did to tissue is seen at the bench. No separate writing is waiting to be shortened.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new removes the watching or the notebook entry.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing the action and judging what it did.
tasks.human_edge: She can tell a real effect on tissue from a stain or a dead patch.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still watches the tissue and still writes the one notebook entry.

reach.learn: Which tissue and matter labels she expects in the notebook.

evidence.claim: Watching living tissue and judging the action on it stays with the person doing the study.
Health data are a special category when the tissue comes from a person.
A works-council rule can treat a log of who did what as a way to observe performance.

assumptions: The observation and the single laboratory notebook entry both stay, so no work is removed. Upkeep is zero because no tool is introduced.
No log of who did what is added, and none is counted as saved time.
If the tissue is from a person, the notebook entry stays in the notebook she already uses and is not sent elsewhere.
unknowns: Whether the tissue is from a person.
research_questions: Is the tissue from a person, and is the notebook the only place that observation is written?

already_counted.description: Watching the tissues and writing the notebook entry stay in full.

incremental.description: No tool is introduced, so upkeep is zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The observation and the notebook entry stay as they are, so the saving is zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Study bacterial growth and structure and the link to health.

steps.what: Study growth, structure, and development of bacteria
Study general characteristics of bacteria and other microorganisms
Judge to understand their relationship to human, plant, and animal health
Compose characteristics sentences from listed growth notes {OTHER}

loop.input: The growth count, structure note, and development note from s1, and the characteristics notes from s2.
loop.output: Sentences that use only those notes.
loop.check: A sentence that names a characteristic or a figure absent from those notes fails.
loop.stop: One short paragraph, or two failed checks, then she writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: The notes are short free text, so a fixed sentence cannot stay inside what she measured.

steps.what: Reject a sentence that adds a characteristic she did not list

tasks.design: The work removed is composing sentences about characteristics from growth, structure, and development notes she has already written, which she does today when she closes the study note in the laboratory notebook {OTHER}. She still studies the bacteria, still records those notes, and still judges the relationship to human, plant, and animal health. The sentences may use only the notes she listed. The health relationship is not composed by the tool. These sentences do not inform on a genetic predisposition.
tasks.previous_blocker: The link to health is a judgement. A sentence that restates her measurements is not that judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Once growth, structure, and development are written as three notes, sentences can stay inside them.
tasks.still_hard: Judging what the characteristics mean for human, plant, and animal health.
tasks.human_edge: She can tell a characteristic that matters for health from one that only looks unusual.
tasks.altitude: She still studies the bacteria and still judges the health relationship. Only the sentences that restate listed characteristics leave, and that composing is writing she does today.

reach.task: Record a growth measurement the study can quote
reach.learn: Write growth, structure, and development as three separate notes.

evidence.claim: A named lab-notebook product drafts notebook entries.
Software that informs on a genetic predisposition can be an in vitro diagnostic device.

assumptions: Today she composes sentences about characteristics from growth, structure, and development notes she has already written. The 12 points on s4 are that composing.
One extra hour per 100 baseline hours keeps the names of those three notes current. That hour is not inside the notes she writes at the bench.
The health judgement stays hers. The sentences do not inform on a genetic predisposition. If those notes are not written down, she composes the sentences herself and the saving is zero.
unknowns: Whether growth, structure, and development are already three written notes or still only in her head.
research_questions: Does she already write characteristics sentences from three measurement notes during the study?

already_counted.description: The growth notes, the characteristics notes, the health judgement, and the sentence check stay in her week.

incremental.description: Keep the names of the growth, structure, and development notes current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the growth, structure, and development notes are not written down she composes the sentences herself and the saving is zero. When they are listed the draft covers that writing only, and one hour goes to keeping the note names, so the high stays at 6.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Investigation, observation, the recommendation, and the health judgement stay hers. The week only loses the first pass over notice abstracts, the first report paragraphs, and the characteristics sentences, and each of those is reading or writing she does today.
reach: An epidemiologist's outbreak-notice review, and which three names a screen may use.
A biological technician's growth-count labels, written as separate notes a sentence can quote.
skills_to_grow: Reject a drafted sentence that adds a result or a characteristic she did not list.
Keep the organism, disease, and antibiotic names current before notices are marked.
role.ambitious_version: She spends the week on which antibiotic effect matters, and the first paragraphs are waiting when she sits down.
